reason: Cymes or corymbs shaped like glomerules are flowers packed into dense clusters. This matches the same batch's mapping of 'glomerulate', 'glomerate' and 'glomerular' to PATO aggregated (EXACT synonym clustered).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: strap-shaped PATO_0002430 – triangular PATO_0001875)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two shapes, read as for 'ovate-lanceolate'. 'Lingulate' already maps to strap-shaped.
Two ovules per locule or carpel is a count, read as for 'uniovulate' and 'multiovulate'.
'Leaves quaternate' means leaves in whorls of four: a whorled arrangement plus a count per node. One term per number would multiply terms needlessly.
Without an awn (arista), as in the rules for 'awnless' (C347) and 'muticous' (C348); 'aristate' is awn present (C207).
Scars, papillae and margins that are not elevated do not stand out from the surface, read as for 'not prominent'. PATO_0001369 raised is defined for microbial colonies, so it does not fit.
An obsolescent petiole, scape or crest is reduced almost to nothing, read as for 'obsolete' (C234) and 'rudimentary'. 'Later obsolescent' keeps its stage through the stage pattern.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (part of the bearer): papilla cell (PO_0025166) of the bearer + glandular (PATO_0002117)
reason: The surface bears papillae that are glandular. This is handled like 'glandular-ciliolate': the gland quality goes on the papillae, so no new term is needed.
Assurgent means curving or rising upwards from a spreading or decumbent base, which is ascending.

reason: Every example states that the orchid column has a foot, so the statement says a part is present, not what a quality is like. The bare word 'foot' was rejected as a generic part, so this needs a 'column foot' bearer class before the rule can be used.

label: nut-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a nut: hard, dry and more or less globose. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991042 cherry-like; for fruits, PO:0030102 nut fruit is the bearer type.
reason: This is the same class proposed for 'nut-like' in batch 0041 of this review. Merge the two spellings into one class.
'Sub-' means 'nearly'. This is the approximate-value pattern, as for 'suborbicular'. 'sublincar' is an OCR misreading of the same word.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (part of the bearer): margin of the bearer + glandular-pubescent (FLOPO:0991173)
reason: The margins carry gland-tipped hairs, read as for 'glandular-ciliolate'. This reuses the glandular hair value on the margin.

label: bigibbous
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being swollen in two places, usually as a pair of pouch-like swellings side by side. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991130 gibbous, which is swollen on one side.
reason: A standard glossary word for nutlets, achene bases and the corolla palate. FLOPO gibbous is defined as swollen on one side, so mapping bigibbous to it would be wrong. A swelling is not a part, so the count pattern does not apply.
Stilt roots are prop roots, as in the bearer rule for 'stilt' in this review. French 'racines-échasses' means the same.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: A comparative ('stronger distally', 'the second pair sometimes stronger') with no fixed value, like 'paler' or 'broader'. When the second term is given, the relation pattern covers it.
Laticiferous means it has laticifers, the latex-bearing cells or canals. 'With latex' says the same. The colour of the latex is a separate statement.

label: ericoid
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of the leaves of heaths (Erica): small, narrow, stiff and often with revolute margins. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002457 leaf-like. For a whole plant, 'ericoid' means it bears such leaves; annotate the leaves.
reason: A widely used resemblance term with no PATO or FLOPO term. It is defined by its leaf form and modelled like other resemblance classes such as scale-like.
Domatiate means it has domatia, usually in the vein axils. The domatium class already exists.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: ovate PATO_0001891 [ovoid] – cylindrical PATO_0001873)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two shapes, read as for 'ovoid-conic' and 'ovoid-globose'.
Slightly prominent veins or reticulation: prominent with the 'sub' qualifier, as for 'suborbicular'.
Leaves, florets or rootstocks 'bunched together' are clustered, an EXACT synonym of aggregated.
Negates FLOPO fibrous for bark, coats and fruit flesh. 'Without fibers' and 'non fibreux' mean the same. On roots, the opposite of 'fibrous-rooted' is a different statement.
Same as 'non-fibrous'. Scales, sheaths and culm bases not breaking into fibres negate FLOPO fibrous.
'Capped by the withered corolla' or 'by tapetal residue' relates the part to another structure on top of it. The covering part is the content, not a quality of the fruit.

label: costapalmate
definition: A fan-shaped quality inhering in a leaf by virtue of the leaf's fan-shaped lamina being traversed by a costa, a prolongation of the petiole into the blade, so that the leaf is intermediate between palmate and pinnate. NOTE: Botany-specific (palms); sibling of FLOPO:0991158 palmately lobed.
reason: A key character of palm leaves with no PATO or FLOPO term. It is a fan-shaped leaf with a costa, so it goes under PATO fan-shaped. 'Weakly' and 'strongly' are degree words handled separately.
Negates FLOPO scarious, used for phyllary, leaf and bract margins.
'Stoloniferous' is the rule stolon present (C208). Its negation is the absence of stolons, like 'awnless'.
'Exceeding the pedicels' or 'the leaves' means longer than another part. It is a relation, and it means nothing without the part it is compared with.
Veins, hair tips and bract apices not forked negate bifurcated, which is also the target for 'dichotomous' (C199).
